sam: ran a quick host-side profile on canary yesterday, ~2k requests across usual mix. observed 3 hotspots: tokenization (avg 6.8ms), request-parsing/serialize (avg 4.2ms), and grpc writev churn causing syscall spikes (~2.5ms). total host overhead ~13.5ms median per request, up from 9.2ms baseline. attaching summaries below.

elaine: ugh, that's a pretty big delta for host overhead. do we have flamegraphs or a raw perf profile?

sam: uploaded perf artifacts to S3: s3://redwood-perf/canary/2734567000/ (perf.data + flame.svg). infra-bot: link: https://s3.redwood.internal/perf/canary/2734567000/flame.svg

paul: quick skim — tokenization dominates on short requests, but for long streaming requests the writev/gRPC batching overhead scales weirdly. looks like repeated small writev calls when chunk size < 1KB.

katie: is that the old per-chunk framing code? We had a change in http2 framing last month to improve latency for 150B chunks; might've regressed for our mixing workloads.

sam: exact. the change added a flush on every incoming chunk when content-length unknown. helps tiny short-chat latency but increases syscall count for streaming long outputs. suggestion: introduce adaptive flush threshold based on predicted output chunk sizes or model kv length.

paul: also saw KV cache eviction storms in the same window. trace shows frequent small requests causing KV cache references to hop shards -> cacheline thrash. could be our host-side key normalization path creating many small keys during chunking.

elaine: can you paste the hot path?

sam: perf top snippet:
```
  22.1%  host:tokenizer::tokenize_utf8
  13.4%  host:parse::frame_and_route
  11.8%  libc::writev (syscall overhead)
  9.6%   host:kvcache::normalize_key
  7.9%   host:serializer::serialize_chunk
```

katie: normalize_key at 9.6% is suspicious — what does it do? concat prefixes, utf8 repr, and a small hash.

paul: idea: memoize normalize_key for incoming request lifecycles (cache per-request) and avoid recomputing across chunk boundaries. cheap LRU per-request should be tiny but help a lot.

elaine: +1. also let's try bumping write coalescing: only flush writes when outstanding buffer >= 2KB or final chunk. that should cut writev syscalls by ~60% for long responses.

sam: proposed quick patch:
```rust
// before: flush_on_chunk = true
flush_on_chunk = chunk.len() >= adaptive_threshold || is_final;
adaptive_threshold = if predicted_out > 2048 { 2048 } else { 512 };
```
will run canary against 1% traffic.

infra-bot: canary deployed to us-west-2 -> canary-flag:host.flush.adaptive=true. rollout id=canary-2734567000.

katie: for kernel selection/batching heuristics: the runtime picks small-kernel for short seqs but we may be falling back to generic kernel because serialization latency widened. patching host-side to return a fast-path hint (expected_max_output_tokens) could allow runtime to avoid expensive kernel handoff. need a small protobuf change + validation.

paul: agree. add a header x-rw-pred-output-tokens that the host can set from tokenizer estimate. runtime can use that in kernel decision. low-risk and measurable.

sam: I'll add telemetry for: writev calls per request, normalize_key hits/misses per request, tokenization latency, and kernel-choice rate. share dashboards in #eng-runtime once data streams in.

elaine: also schedule a microbenchmark: 5k synthetic streams with heavy chunking to validate write coalescing patch. put results in the artifact bucket.

sam: running the microbench now — sending initial numbers in ~30m. preliminary expectation: host overhead down to ~8-9ms median if both patches land. :crossed_fingers:

katie: if we see KV cache still thrashing after memoization, consider sharded key namespaces by request-id prefix to improve locality. rough plan but add as fallback.

paul: noted. thanks everyone — if the canary looks good we'll promote and follow up with kernel hint PR.

sam: thanks. ping me if you want access to traces or need to run the bench locally (docker image: docker.pkg.redwood/runtime-bench:latest).

infra-bot: canary metrics being collected: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/ingress/canary-2734567000 (expect ~10m to populate). :hourglass_flowing_sand:
